meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 3: Server Concepts (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about subscriptions/listen are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A graceful server shutdown simply drops the stream without a response
The first message on the stream is notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
It replaces resources/subscribe, which remains available for single-resource watches
The acknowledgment lists only the notification types the server agreed to honour
The subscriptionId in each notification equals the JSON-RPC id of the listen request

questions.explanation: A, B and C are the mechanics. subscriptions/listen fully replaces resources/subscribe and resources/unsubscribe, which no longer exist, and a graceful close sends the listen request's own result before closing: a drop without that result signals an unexpected disconnect.

questions.question: Which statements about resources and prompts are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Servers must list every resource a tool might return as a resource_link
Resource templates use RFC 6570 URI templates and support argument completion
A missing required prompt argument is reported as -32602 Invalid params
Resources are model-controlled: the model chooses which URIs to read
prompts/get may return an InputRequiredResult if the server needs more input

questions.explanation: Templates support completion, prompts/get is one of the three MRTR-eligible requests, and bad prompt arguments are -32602. Resources are application-controlled, and resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in resources/list.

questions.question: Your server needs a shopping cart to survive across tool calls. Which practices match the spec's guidance? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Generate the handle with a secure random source and give it a bounded lifetime
Treat possession of the handle as proof of identity for unauthenticated callers
Authorize the caller against the handle on every call, keyed by the verified user
Return an explicit handle from a creation tool and accept it as an argument later
Keep the cart in memory keyed by the connection, since one client owns one connection

questions.explanation: MCP has no protocol session, so cross-call state uses explicit handles. A handle is a name, not a credential: servers MUST NOT treat possession as authentication and SHOULD bind state to the authenticated user. Keying by connection is exactly what statelessness forbids.
